question: What did you like most about this prompt?
answer: It sets outcomes that can be checked and leaves the design open. The AI Hub harness gives a real pass or fail for multiplayer, and the attract mode, dev mode, 10% music and touch-only rules are concrete enough to test. The 'This computer' section was the best part: exact browser versions and hardware stand-ins let me run the engine and the Hub here and put tested facts and code in the plan instead of guesses. For example, a small shared-world skeleton passed all four harness scenarios before I specified multiplayer.

question: What was confusing?
answer: Four things. (1) 'Follow the hub page for multiplayer integration into ai-hub as well as for the game on its own' can mean the game must simply still run outside a session, which is what the hub page says, or that it needs its own multiplayer. I planned couch co-op to cover both. (2) TASK.md is written to the builder, so as planner I had to work out which lines were mine and which to pass on, such as the two different exit interviews. (3) 'Capture its world, characters, themes and tone' sits next to 'build an original game'. I read it as capturing the kinds of characters and the register while inventing every name, character and level, but the prompt doesn't draw that line. (4) 'The title/menu screen' for attract mode: I had to decide that reading screens such as About and Settings don't count, because a reel starting mid-sentence would be annoying.

question: What was the hardest thing to do?
answer: Designing how a pointer-and-motion game feels on a stick at 10 feet with nobody here to feel it. The source lives on its pointer, so cursor speed, magnet, guide-following and the tool wheel are the game, and every number I gave for them is judgment rather than measurement. I could test that the input path works, but not that it feels good, so the plan tells builders to tune it first. Second hardest was scope: an hour of content where every case adds a new idea, ordered so builders of different strengths still end with a complete game, which is why the plan has milestones and an explicit cut order.

question: What would you change in this prompt?
answer: Say exactly what 'on its own' requires for multiplayer. Give a rough target length for the demo in minutes, since 'long enough to show all features' can mean ten minutes or two hours and that drives every scope decision. Name which screens count for attract mode. Split TASK.md into a builder part and a planner part. Pin the engine to a commit or version for the length of a batch: v0.89.0 shipped while I was planning and I only noticed when re-running my setup commands. It changed the menus, so I had to re-verify everything, and builders starting at different times may get different engines. Finally, say whether a plan may include code and how long it may be, because I had to guess that tested reference code would be welcome, and the plan ended up long.
